whatItIs.text: Milk from dairy cows — the reference liquid the food world measures everything against; international standards have defined it as an unadulterated mammary secretion since 1961.

historyNote.text: As an adult food, milk is a biological newcomer: most adults originally lacked the enzyme to digest its lactose, and milk drinking spread only where a genetic quirk for digesting it spread among dairying cultures.

howToChoose.text: Check the date and grab from the coldest part of the chiller; whole, semi-skimmed, and skimmed differ mainly in fat, so match to the recipe — whole milk for custards and baking, skimmed where richness does not matter.

storage.text: Keep in the main body of the fridge, not the door, and never return unused milk from a jug. The rulebook has the storage window and spoilage signs.
storage.note: dairy storage windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Milk on the turn is still useful: bake it into pancakes or scones, simmer into rice pudding, or freeze cubes for coffee — sour baked-goods milk (not off-smelling milk) is what buttermilk does anyway.

substitutions.note: closest dairy-free swap for sauces and baking; slightly sweet
